name: dn-empty-rdn-embedded-invalid
description: The leaf subject contains an RDN with zero AVAs (an empty SET) wedged between C=US and CN=Alice. X.501 defines an RDN as a SET OF AttributeTypeAndValue and does not explicitly forbid the empty SET, but the X.501 abstract model treats every RDN as a non-empty selector for a directory entry; every interoperable encoder we know of rejects emitting one. The permitted-subtrees constraint is C=US,O=Example, and a leaf containing an empty RDN cannot match it under RFC 5280 7.1 (the matching RDN at index 1 has 0 attributes, the constraint's has 1), so the leaf is outside the permitted subtree.
notes: Constructed via subject_der_ascii2der. Different parsers handle the empty SET differently: some reject the cert outright as malformed DER; some accept and treat the empty RDN as 'no constraint' for that position (collapsing the prefix length); some accept and propagate the zero-AVA RDN through to comparison. Each of these has different security implications for constraint matching and CN-fallback hostname checks.

certs.subject: C=US,O=Example,CN=Alice
certs.subject_der_ascii2der: SEQUENCE { SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.6 } PrintableString { "US" } } } SET { } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.3 } UTF8String { "Alice" } } } }
